purpose: Define how two property fixture governance snapshots are compared while preserving historical truth and separating technical state changes from legal changes.
rules: A later snapshot does not rewrite an earlier snapshot.
Technical governance transitions must not be presented as legal conclusions.
A legal-source status transition requires separate legal-change evidence.
A production-evidence transition requires actual evidence records.
Publication-status changes require their independent publication gate.
If snapshots conflict on historical identity or capture date, comparison is BLOCKED.
Synthetic fixture changes remain within technical fixture governance unless separately promoted through approved evidence governance.
guardrails: Snapshot comparison is not legal analysis.
It does not prove ownership, title, boundary or any other property fact.
It does not represent live official-record retrieval.
